title: Retain Entra authentication after a SQL driver upgrade
goal: Restore built-in Entra authentication for EF SQL Server and SQL distributed cache when upgrading to SqlClient 7, preserving the intended host identity.

selectionNotes: EF SQL Server and SQL distributed cache share this dependency-migration goal. SqlClient 6.1.7 includes built-in Entra providers; SqlClient 7.1.0 requires the directly referenced matching Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.Extensions.Azure 7.1.0 for driver-managed Active Directory authentication. Active Directory Default selects credentials available to the host; review that selection explicitly. Replace obsolete Active Directory Password with a supported host-appropriate flow. No password mode is retained in these samples. Application-supplied AccessToken/AccessTokenCallback does not require this extension merely to supply a token.

prerequisites: Restore the pinned projects with their matching SDKs. For --connect, supply MARSH_SQL_CONNECTION with Active Directory Default and an authorized identity/target; precreate dbo.ObservationCache and grant the minimum cache DML permissions. Never use production resources. Run eng/Test-MarshAccess.ps1 for both configuration/provider checks without connecting. Maintainers can repeat the approved PIN-679 isolated route with eng/Test-MarshEntra.ps1 -Record, which revokes temporary grants and removes its cache table; -CheckEvidence performs only read-only freshness checks.
stabilityLimitations: Stable SqlClient authentication APIs; EF/cache11 GA artifacts on SDK11 GA require GA reconciliation under PIN-965. Certificate-backed Default route verified; interactive/MFA and managed/workload identity untested.
